fields.why: Age-adjusted prevalences are compared across 7 race groups, 5 age groups, employment and education levels, with t-tests stated for subgroup differences.

Race (7 groups, lower four vs higher three), age (>=65 vs other groups), employment (unable to work, unemployed vs employed) and education (college vs the rest) are SPDs with 3+ groups compared; sex has 2 and marital status is not an SPD.

The brief names this case: a blanket 't-tests' statement ('All indicated differences between subgroups are statistically significant') under 'lower/highest compared with' claims is per-group vs referent only.
